title: Tested bytecode != deployable bytecode: story-031 pins via_ir=false for every build this repo performs, while phStaging (the established deploy vehicle) compiles with via_ir=true
description: The 365-test suite only ever executes LEGACY-codegen bytecode (phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml:15 pins via_ir = false), while phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml:7 sets via_ir = true -- BOTH VERIFIED IN SOURCE. The two pipelines emit a measured 1,450 B / ~9% runtime bytecode delta (15,979 B legacy vs 14,529 B via_ir). PhlimboV3 therefore has ZERO test coverage of the bytecode that would actually be deployed. This is an ASSURANCE GAP, explicitly NOT an attack path: no defect is demonstrated and none is claimed.
attackPath: NOT AN ATTACK PATH -- recorded as an assurance gap with no demonstrated root cause.
conditions: Prospective: PhlimboV3 is not yet wired into phStaging.
recommendation: Either (a) set via_ir = true in phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml so tests execute deployable codegen, or (b) gate the V3 deploy story on a via_ir test run. Option (a) is cheap -- see USEFUL_NEGATIVE_RESULTS.

USEFUL_NEGATIVE_RESULTS.note: These outputs are MORE VALUABLE than the finding's severity and MUST survive any downgrade.
USEFUL_NEGATIVE_RESULTS.eip170: EIP-170 IS GENUINELY RESOLVED and is INDEPENDENT of via_ir. The via_ir build fits MORE comfortably (14,529 B, +10,047 B margin) than the legacy build (15,979 B, +8,597 B margin). So via_ir = false is NOT load-bearing for the size limit and can be revisited freely without reopening it. This is a hard, checkable fact that makes the preferred fix cheap -- and it directly REBUTS the reasoning in phlimbo-ea/foundry.toml's own comment block ('fits EIP-170...').
USEFUL_NEGATIVE_RESULTS.v3Unwired: PhlimboV3 has ZERO references anywhere in phoenix-phase-2-staging (full-list grep, NOT truncated -- per the project's grep|head rule, since this is a negative claim; PhlimboV2 matches 36 files for contrast). phStaging pins lib/phlimbo-ea at 6cb0bc0c, a commit whose src/ predates PhlimboV3.sol entirely. PhlimboV3 is undeployed and unwired -- the 'prospective, not live' framing is correct.

SEVERITY_DISAGREEMENT_IN_BAND.recorded: Deliberately recorded in-band rather than silently picking a side.

validityChecker.verdict: QUESTIONED -- RETAIN but RECOMMEND Low -> QA, reframed as a GATE on the V3 deploy story rather than a finding against the code ('PhlimboV3 has zero test coverage of deployable bytecode').
reasoning: SPECULATION (detected): the prospective leg is conditional on a wiring that DOES NOT EXIST; the finding's own step 3 is explicitly conditional ('IF PhlimboV3 is wired into phStaging') and its residual risk is admittedly generic ('via_ir is a distinct Yul codegen pipeline with its own historical miscompilation record'). The finding says so itself: 'NOT AN ATTACK PATH', 'No defect demonstrated'.

It is a demonstrated PROCESS gap about a PROSPECTIVE deploy, not a speculated VULNERABILITY. That is a real category and worth keeping -- it is simply not a security finding, and the Low label implies one.
validityChecker.counterweight_acknowledgedByValidityChec: The speculation pattern does NOT bite cleanly: what IS demonstrated is demonstrated empirically, in code that exists TODAY. 'Speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' bars inventing a bug in code that does not exist; this finding does the OPPOSITE -- it demonstrates a measured divergence between two files that both exist today, and then explicitly DECLINES to invent a bug.

severityAuditor.reasoning: Correctly declines to invent a defect -- inventing one would be the actual violation. The measured codegen divergence against the established deploy vehicle that already ships Phlimbo V1/V2 is a real, demonstrated root cause OF THE ASSURANCE GAP.
severityAuditor.authority: The severity-auditor OWNS severity, so Low STANDS.

SEVERITY_DISAGREEMENT_IN_BAND.resolution: HELD AT LOW per the severity-auditor. The validity-checker's QA recommendation and reasoning are recorded here and on the ledger entry, unresolved and visible, for human triage.
